subject: Trial governance & performance acceptance — next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sam Durand <sam.durand@olive-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Trial governance & performance acceptance — next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so we have alignment before we kick off the trial:

Summary of objectives:
- Validate that Redwood can meet your latency and throughput targets for the analytics summarization pipeline (target p50 latency < 120ms for 512-token prompts; sustained throughput ~120 reqs/sec).
- Demonstrate cost efficiency with our quantized model profile (target < $0.0009 per token on typical workload).
- Maintain generation quality above your QA threshold (BLEU-like/qualitative pass rate >= 92% on your benchmark set).

Proposed POC structure (high level):
1) Week 0 (prep) — load representative dataset + share sample workload spec (you promised a CSV of 500 sample requests).
2) Week 1 (baseline) — smoke tests and baseline profiling on your sample workload (latency/throughput/cost).
3) Week 2 (tuning) — apply batching, cache hints, and quantization profile recommended by Redwood Optimize; re-run measurements.
4) Week 3 (validation) — run acceptance tests against your QA prompt set and review results.

Success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 260ms (512-token avg).
- Throughput: sustained 120 rps with <= 20% tail amplification under burst.
- Cost per token: amortized <= $0.0009/token using recommended config.
- Quality: >= 92% pass rate on your QA rubric; no critical functional regressions.

Owners and asks:
- Olive: provide sample workload CSV + QA rubric by Wed 4/21.
- Redwood (me): deliver POC template and environment details (attached) by EOD Mon 4/19.
- Marcus (SE): will own tuning knobs and run perf tests; Ben will own commercial checkpoints and licensing discussions. Monica will coordinate CS handoff on validation.

Attachments: redwood-poc-template.xlsx (POC checklist & runbook).

If that matches your expectations, confirm the sample dataset delivery date and I’ll book a 30m kickoff for Mon 4/26.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com | +1 415-555-0134

Subject: Re: Trial governance & performance acceptance — next steps

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear recap. That aligns with what we discussed. Two clarifications before we lock dates:
1) The 120 rps sustained — is that measured per model instance or end-to-end through your routing layer? We plan to simulate concurrent end-users hitting a single endpoint.
2) For quality, our rubric is a mix of automated checks and manual review. The 92% target is fine, but can we define what constitutes a "critical functional regression" (e.g., hallucination on named entity extraction > 5%)?

We can commit to delivering the sample workload CSV and the QA rubric by Wed 4/21. Procurement (procurement@olive-analytics.com) has a couple questions about the trial data handling — I’m looping them in on the next thread.

We’re good to target a Mon 4/26 kickoff; prefer afternoon Pacific.

Thanks —
Sam Durand
Director of Product — Olive Analytics
sam.durand@olive-analytics.com | +1 212-555-0199

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial governance & performance acceptance — next steps

Sam — great, thank you. Quick answers and a slightly tightened acceptance definition so we can make objective calls at validation:

1) Throughput measurement: we will measure sustained RPS at the endpoint level from our load generator against the deployed endpoint (this includes the routing layer); we will call out instance-level metrics separately (VM/GPU utilization) but the acceptance gate is endpoint-level sustainment.

2) Critical regression definition (proposed): any regression that causes >5% drop in your QA pass rate on a given category (NER, factual extraction, summarization fidelity), or any single failure mode that causes data corruption/incorrect structure in >2% of outputs. Hallucination threshold example: >5% incorrect named-entity insertions on the NER benchmark triggers a fail.

Operational notes:
- Marcus will run the initial perf sweep Wed 4/28. We’ll share Grafana dashboards and a live dashboard link.
- Ben, can you confirm the commercial checkpoint cadence? I propose a mid-POC check (end of Week 1) and a final decision review (end of Week 3).

Procurement, welcome — happy to join a quick call to go over data handling. We are happy to sign an NDA; standard trial agreement covers logs retention and ephemeral data handling.

Next steps: I’ll attach the workload template again and draft an acceptance checklist reflecting the definitions above. Confirm afternoon PT on Mon 4/26 and I’ll send calendar invite.

Best,
Vanessa

Subject: Internal: Ops owners & validation runbook (Olive Analytics POC)

Vanessa / Ben / Marcus —

Internal ops note to capture owners and the validation runbook items before the kickoff. Posting here so we have a single source of truth:

Owners:
- Test lead / perf sweeps: Marcus Lin (SE) — runbook, load generator configs, dashboard links.
- Data onboarding & QA rubric checks: Monica Patel (CS) — will coordinate manual review and acceptance scoring.
- Commercial checkpoints: Ben Carter (AE) — mid-POC and final.
- Escalation / SLA exceptions: Vanessa Ortiz (AE lead) 

Validation runbook (high level):
1) Ingest sample CSV (olive-sample-workload-specs.csv) into the sandbox endpoint.
2) Baseline run: 10-minute steady-state @ 30 rps, record p50/p95 latency, token counts, and cost estimates.
3) Scale run: 60 / 120 / 180 rps bursts (5m each) to capture tail behavior.
4) Tuning pass: apply batching and KV cache hints. Re-run scale run.
5) Quality sweep: run QA rubric on 500 items (mix of automated assertions + 50 manual reviews).
6) Acceptance: apply pass thresholds (latency, throughput, cost, quality) and produce an acceptance report.

I’ve attached the sample workload spec to this email thread for convenience. Marcus, I’ll need the Grafana link and the exact load-generator command by Tue EOD.

Thanks —
Monica
